solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fix the car before start of arrangements for air passage

indicators.note: to fix the car here is to rework it, so its letters are put in a new order
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is taken from arrangements

explanation.surface: A motorist is told to repair the vehicle before making plans for some airflow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' rearranges THE CAR into TRACHE; 'start of' adds the A of 'arrangements'.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is the tube carrying breath to the lungs, a literal air passage.

clue.text: Part of farm captured by those on the outside

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so the farm word sits within the other letters
the letters on the outside of a word are its first and last, here taken from those

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle

explanation.surface: Part of a farm has been seized by outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' gives TE, the ends of 'those', which hold RANCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice of something, such as a share issue.

clue.text: Fat individual taken in by modern-day attitude

indicators.note: to be taken in is to be enclosed, so one letter goes inside the others

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
a pose is a posture or affected attitude
I is a single person, one individual

explanation.surface: A fat person is absorbed by today's way of thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the adjective for fatty tissue, so it means fat in the bodily sense.

clue.text: They may be kicked when doing nothing

definitions.text: They may be kicked when doing nothing

parts.words: They may be kicked when doing nothing
parts.note: the idiom for waiting about idly is kicking one's ___, naming body parts at the back of the feet

explanation.definitionFit: To kick one's heels is an idiom for waiting idly with nothing to do.

clue.text: Clear writer with one's signature at the end

parts.note: an author is a writer
one's means one is, giving I and S

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here the last of signature

explanation.surface: A writer is approved once they put their name at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', I + S; 'at the end' takes the E of 'signature'.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear something is to give official approval or permission for it.

clue.text: Cats, say, showing noted talent

definitions.meaning: Cats is an example of a stage show built on song
gifted at music, the notes being ... ones

explanation.definitionFit: Cats is a stage show with songs, and someone gifted with melody is described with the same adjective.

clue.text: Force jet fighter over height

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over, above, the second

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian jet fighter

explanation.surface: A jet fighter flies high above the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or power, a synonym for force.

clue.text: Merchant in store at works

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new shape, as material is worked

explanation.surface: A trader is employed in the shop at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges IN STORE AT; the word looks like a noun, a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a merchant who sells paper and writing materials.

clue.text: Marx comes across silver in city

indicators.note: one piece spans across another, enclosing it

parts.note: Chico was one of the Marx Brothers comedians
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A Marx brother finds some silver in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a large city in Illinois, USA.

clue.text: Stores fat with shows of hesitation

parts.note: lard is pig fat
er is the sound people make when hesitating, here plural

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly hoards fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Larders are rooms or cupboards where food is stored, so stores in the noun sense.

clue.text: A fruit not cored provides nutritious substance

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: a cored word loses its middle, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A fruit that has not been cored is good to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cored' empties 'not' to leave N and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment.

clue.text: Craftsman who's not so keen on working after golf

indicators.note: the description follows the golf letter

parts.note: golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lazier means less inclined to work

explanation.surface: A tradesman who prefers to idle after a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a craftsman who fits glass into windows.

clue.text: Panicky sort of cow in eye line

indicators.note: panicky letters are in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous kind of cow is spotted in someone's line of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's feet are the fine wrinkles at the outer corner of the eye, lines by the eye.

clue.text: Charge after one, spitting feathers

indicators.note: the charge word comes after the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Someone is incensed after being charged once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitting feathers' is British slang for being furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spitting feathers is a British idiom for being very angry.

clue.text: Angry men expect to hold back opposition

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in reverse
the clue words hold the run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Furious men anticipate keeping their rivals at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' finds YMENE in 'angrY MEN Expect'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The enemy is the opposing side, the opposition in a conflict.

clue.text: Song causing dry eyes at being played?

indicators.note: letters being played are performed in a new arrangement, like a tune reworked

explanation.surface: A tune that leaves no tear in the eye when performed?
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday is a famous Beatles song.

clue.text: Naive, but clever replacing one eye for you, say

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the word for clever

parts.note: ingenious means clever and inventive
one eye spoken sounds like the letter I
you spoken sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone simple but smart swaps one eye for yours.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Is in INGENIOUS (the letter that sounds like 'eye') becomes U (sounds like 'you').
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuous means innocent and unsuspecting, a synonym of naive.

clue.text: He got a different purpose for lodge

indicators.note: a different form of the words means their letters are reordered

parts.note: use is purpose or function

explanation.surface: A man found another purpose for his cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges HE GOT A into GATEHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatehouse is a lodge at the gate of an estate.

clue.text: Anxiety putting slow cadet into a tizzy?

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of confusion, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A sluggish trainee panics.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold sweat is the clammy perspiration of fear, so a state of anxiety.

clue.text: Follow offender's record

parts.note: a con is a convict, an offender
form is slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: Fall into line, as a criminal's history suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to follow rules or customs.

clue.text: Stand made by Hannibal, west of Turin

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the killer in The Silence of the Lambs

indicators.note: meant to pick a single edge letter of Turin; the setter has chosen the wrong side

explanation.surface: A stand built by the Carthaginian general just west of an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The general with elephants is a decoy. The N needed is the last letter of Turin, its east end, not its west, as the blog also notes; the setter slipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a stand from which someone reads or speaks.

clue.text: Party animal beginning to riot, say

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from riot

parts.note: to aver is to state or say

explanation.surface: A wild partygoer starts a riot, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who parties wildly, a party animal.

clue.text: A train breaks down after five — that's different!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters follow the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: a train that breaks down is wrecked, its letters scattered

explanation.surface: A train fails after five o'clock, which makes a change!
explanation.definitionFit: Variant as an adjective means differing from the standard form.

clue.text: Told of consanguinity!

definitions.meaning: told, as of a story recounted
linked by blood, belonging to the same family

explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell it, and kin are connected by blood, family members.

clue.text: French city welcomes hotel for specialist market

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the city letters enclose the hotel

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A city on the Riviera opens its doors to a hotel aimed at a narrow clientele.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a small specialised segment of a market.

clue.text: Surprisingly help a mere transient

indicators.note: the letters turn out in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Unexpectedly, a mere vagrant gets some help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges HELP A MERE; 'transient' looks like a noun, a drifter, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time, short-lived.

clue.text: Better people in education

indicators.note: the people word goes in the education abbreviation

parts.note: men can mean people, staff

explanation.surface: Men in education are improved.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it, better it.

clue.text: Language used when in post, mainly

indicators.note: the when word goes inside the shortened post word
mainly means most of it, the word minus its last letter

parts.note: post means mail
as can mean when, as in as he left

explanation.surface: A language that's used chiefly when posting letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims MAIL to MAI, which holds AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Masai (Maa) is the language of the Masai people of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Late deliveries expected

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler
due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: Parcels expected haven't arrived yet.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler's deliveries (balls) come in sets of six called overs.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means past the expected time, late.

clue.text: Increases price of bitter for one who's pretentious

parts.note: a seller who ups a price raises it
tart means sharp or bitter in taste

explanation.surface: A pub raises what it charges for a pint of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British beer, but here it is a taste.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen who acts with self-importance.

clue.text: Half of Monaco looked loaded

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: Someone in Monaco checked things out and looked rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means wealthy, and loaded is slang for very rich.

clue.text: Went out to protect son, but had a life

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the son letter sits inside

parts.note: exited means went out

explanation.surface: Someone left to shield their boy, yet still lived.
explanation.definitionFit: To have existed is to have lived, had a life.
